summary: The runtime canary verified the evidence boundary rather than inventing concurrency. A historical QA-precompile execution has durable PIN, STARTED and RETURN endpoints from 20:10:14Z to 20:12:14Z (120000 ms), but no producer execution is durably bound to the same delivery unit. Therefore the parent fixture's 1250 ms serial / 750 ms modeled parallel / 40% reduction remains simulation evidence only. The canary adds an observability-only evaluator and regression that requires a shared explicit delivery_unit_ref before computing overlap, serial baseline or real critical path. QA-precompile remains advisory-only and outside promotion fan-in; blocker failure still forces promotion_ready=false while a reversible candidate can remain usable, without creating new scheduling or promotion authority.

feature_evidence.evidence: QA-precompile has a durable 120000 ms interval, but no producer shares an explicit durable delivery_unit_ref. Runtime overlap is therefore not proven and is emitted as insufficient comparable evidence.

feature_evidence.evidence: Regression enforces blocker FAIL => promotion_ready=false and candidate usable=true; parent deterministic failure canary independently records the same guarded behavior.

truth_boundary: This return verifies the runtime evidence boundary, not distributed concurrency. It does not claim a real 40% reduction, does not infer a producer from unrelated workers, and grants no scheduler, liveness, CURRENT, Human Accepted, Served or promotion authority.
unresolved: A future comparable canary needs an existing durable event owner to bind producer and QA-precompile to the same delivery_unit_ref.
Both comparable units need durable STARTED and completion endpoints before overlap, serial baseline and real critical path can be measured.
